content.text: Hi! I'd like to try out what this viewer can do.

content.thinking:
They want to try the features.
I'll briefly show what can be displayed.
Common markdown elements will make the styling easy to see.

Elements to show:
- bold, italic, strikethrough
- inline code, code blocks
- quotes, links
- lists

content.text:
Hi! Common markdown elements are supported:

**bold**, *italic*, ~~strikethrough~~, `inline code`, [a link](https://github.com)

> Block quotes work too

Click the Thinking pill above to expand or collapse my reasoning.
What about code blocks?

content.thinking:
Show a code block example.
A small JavaScript function will do.

content.text: I have a question today.
Sure, go ahead.
(A day later) I'm back.

content.thinking:
They came back a day later.
A date divider should appear above, which checks multi-day rendering.

content.text:
Welcome back! Did you notice the two date dividers above? That's how a conversation spanning several days looks.

Both days are highlighted in the Timeline; click one to see the conversations from that day.
Show me a message with lots of thinking blocks.

content.thinking:
First thought.
They want to see how several thinking blocks look.

Second thought.
Blocks should be separated by spacing only, with no dashes or rules.

Third thought.
This checks the spacing between blocks.

Fourth thought.
The pill should show a count of 4.

content.text: The pill above shows 4 thinking blocks. Expand it and you'll see they are separated only by white space, with no dividing lines.
What's the advantage of a list comprehension over a for loop?

content.thinking: This is a basic concept; lead with the answer, then one small example.

content.text: Mostly brevity: `[x*2 for x in nums]` says "double every element" in one line. It's usually a little faster too, since the loop runs inside the interpreter. When the logic gets complex, a plain for loop reads better.
Should I use git merge or rebase?

content.thinking: The usual confusion is when to use which, so answer by situation.

content.text:
A simple rule:

- **merge** keeps the real branch history; use it when merging into shared branches
- **rebase** makes the history a straight line; use it to tidy commits you haven't pushed yet

Don't rebase a branch that's already pushed and used by others.
Got it, thanks!
You're welcome, ask any time.
What does this error mean: `IndexError: list index out of range`
You accessed an index past the end of the list. If the list has 3 items, the highest index is 2, but the code asked for `items[3]`. Try `print(len(items))` to see the real length.
Thanks, that's really helpful ✨
Glad it helped.
What's the difference between `.*?` and `.*` in a regex?

content.thinking: Comparing both on one concrete string shows it best.

content.text: `.*` is greedy and takes as many characters as it can; `.*?` is lazy and stops at the shortest match. On `<a><b>`, `<.*>` matches the whole string while `<.*?>` matches just `<a>`.
My SQL query is slow. Where do I start?

Run `EXPLAIN` and look for full table scans. Common fixes: index the columns used in WHERE and JOIN, avoid wrapping indexed columns in functions, and select only the columns you need instead of `SELECT *`.
How do I vertically center an element with flexbox?

content.thinking: A snippet they can copy will help most.

content.text: Thanks, that's really helpful
Glad it helped.
My code has a long if/elif chain that returns a different message for each type. How can I simplify it?
Map types to messages with a dictionary: `MESSAGES = {'a': '…', 'b': '…'}`, then `MESSAGES.get(kind, 'default message')`. Adding a new type then takes one line.
OK, thanks! 😊
Any time.
What should I watch out for when writing a scraper?
A few things: read the site's robots.txt and terms first; space out your requests so you don't load their server; handle errors and retries; and only use the data in ways you're allowed to.
OK, thanks!
Any time.
How do I tell affect and effect apart?

content.thinking: A memory aid will stick better than a grammar rule here.

content.text: Most of the time **affect** is the verb and **effect** is the noun. A memory aid: *A for action*, so the action word is affect.
Can you make this sentence sound more natural: I very like this book.

content.thinking: One rewritten example says more than an explanation.

content.text: Try *I really like this book.* or *I like this book a lot.* — very can't modify a verb directly.
What's a safe way to open an argumentative essay?
One reliable shape: one sentence restating the question, one sentence stating your position. Clear beats fancy.
Got it, thanks!
You're welcome, ask any time.
I want to get better at speaking. How should I plan each day?
About 20 minutes: 5 minutes shadowing a recording, 10 minutes talking to yourself about one topic while recording, 5 minutes listening back for mistakes. Consistency matters more than length.
Got it, thanks!
You're welcome, ask any time.
What can I use instead of Best regards to end an email?
Common ones are *Kind regards*, *Many thanks* and *Cheers* (more casual). *Kind regards* is the safest in formal settings.
What comes after look forward to?
A noun or an -ing form: *I look forward to hearing from you.* The to here is a preposition, not part of an infinitive.
Is by the way fine in a formal email?
It works but sounds conversational. *Additionally* or *Also* reads a bit more formal.
For tomato and egg stir-fry, do the eggs or the tomatoes go first?

Eggs first: pour them into hot oil and take them out when they're about 70% set. Then cook the tomatoes until they release their juice and fold the eggs back in. The eggs stay tender and the sauce stays juicy.
Thanks, that's really helpful
Glad it helped.
I only have eggs, potatoes and an onion. What can I make?

content.thinking: They have few ingredients, so suggest one dish they can make right now.

content.text: A Spanish tortilla: slice the potato and onion thinly and cook them gently until soft, pour in the beaten eggs, let it set over low heat, then flip and cook two more minutes.
How long should I preheat the oven?
Usually 10–15 minutes, until the indicator says it has reached temperature. For cakes and other temperature-sensitive bakes, make sure it's fully preheated.
OK, thanks! 😊
Any time.
My rice keeps coming out undercooked. What am I doing wrong?
Usually too little water or no soaking. Use about 1:1.2 rice to water, soak for 20 minutes, and let it rest covered for 10 minutes after cooking.
OK, thanks!
Any time.
Any dinner I can make in 15 minutes?
Scallion oil noodles: cook the noodles, pour hot oil over chopped scallions, soy sauce and a pinch of sugar, then toss. Add a fried egg and it's a full meal.
Thanks, that's really helpful
Glad it helped.
How do I keep stir-fried greens bright green?
High heat and a quick toss in a properly hot pan; salt at the end; or blanch them for 10 seconds first.
Thanks, that's really helpful
Glad it helped.
How can I plan three days in Kyoto without rushing?

content.thinking: An itinerary reads best split by area.

content.text: Split it by area: day one Higashiyama (Kiyomizu-dera, Ninenzaka), day two Arashiyama, day three Fushimi Inari plus the city centre. Head out early to beat the crowds.
Got it, thanks!
You're welcome, ask any time.
What should I know about driving in Iceland?
Watch the weather and road conditions (check road.is before setting off); F-roads need four-wheel drive; petrol stations can be far apart, so fill up at half a tank.
OK, thanks!
Any time.
What's easiest to forget on a short trip?
Chargers, regular medication, copies of your documents and a folding shopping bag. Keep a fixed checklist and run through it each time.
Thanks, that's really helpful
Glad it helped.
How do I take better travel photos?
Use early morning and late afternoon light; don't always centre people, try the rule of thirds; take a few shots and pick the best.
Got it, thanks! ✨
You're welcome, ask any time.
Is travel insurance worth it for a trip abroad?
Yes, especially medical cover and delay protection. Check the exclusions for higher-risk activities.
OK, thanks!
Any time.

name: Names in One Hundred Years of Solitude

content.text: There are too many names in One Hundred Years of Solitude. Any tips?
Sketch a family tree as you go, or keep a printed one beside you. Halfway through you'll notice the repeating names are part of the point.
I never have time to read. How do I keep going?

content.thinking: They need a method they can act on, not general advice.

content.text: Make the goal small: 10 pages a day, or 15 minutes before bed. Carry a book with you so spare minutes count.
Thanks, that's really helpful ✨
Glad it helped.
Can you recommend a few popular science books for beginners?
Try *A Brief History of Time*, *The Selfish Gene* and *Sapiens*. They cover different ground, so start with the one that interests you most.
OK, thanks!
Any time.
How do I take reading notes that are actually useful?
Don't just copy quotes. After each chapter, write three sentences in your own words: what it said, what you agree with, and where you could use it.
Paper books or e-books?
Each has its strengths: paper is easier to focus on and flip back through; e-books are easy to carry and search. It depends on where you usually read.
Thanks, that's really helpful
Glad it helped.
I've never run before. How do I start?
Start with run-walk intervals: run 1 minute, walk 2, repeat 8 times. Three times a week, and gradually lengthen the running parts.
What can I do at home without equipment?
Squats, push-ups, planks and lunges. Three sets of each with a minute of rest between sets.
OK, thanks! 😊
Any time.
My knee hurts a bit after running. Is that normal?

content.thinking: This involves pain, so mention seeing a doctor when needed.

content.text: Mild soreness can just be your body adjusting, but sharp or lasting pain means stop and see a doctor. Check your shoes and stride length too.
OK, thanks!
Any time.
How long should I stretch after a workout?
20–30 seconds per area, focusing on the front and back of the thighs, calves and glutes; 5–10 minutes in total is plenty.
Got it, thanks!
You're welcome, ask any time.
I can't fall asleep at night. What helps?
Keep a regular wake-up time, put screens away an hour before bed, and skip coffee after lunch. If it goes on for a long time, talk to a doctor.
Got it, thanks! 🙏
You're welcome, ask any time.
Can you design a meeting notes template for me?

content.thinking: Give a structure they can reuse as is.

content.text:
It could include:

1. Date and attendees
2. Topics
3. Decisions
4. Action items (owner + due date)

The action items matter most.
My weekly updates read like a diary. How do I fix that?
Use three parts: results, problems, next week's plan, with only the two or three most important points in each. Use numbers wherever you can.
Got it, thanks!
You're welcome, ask any time.
I have too much to do. What comes first?
Sort things roughly by urgent and important, and do the important-and-urgent ones first. Schedule the important-but-not-urgent ones ahead of time, or they'll turn urgent.
How much text should one slide have?
One idea per slide, with the conclusion as the title. Keep the body to three lines or fewer and put details in your speaker notes.
OK, thanks!
Any time.
Why are my pothos leaves turning yellow?
Usually too much water or too little light. Water only once the topsoil is dry and move it somewhere with bright, indirect light.
My friend loves painting. What's a good birthday gift?
A good set of watercolours, a sketchbook, or a trial class. A handwritten card makes it more personal.
Thanks, that's really helpful
Glad it helped.
What should I practise first on guitar?
A few basic chords: C, G, Am and F (F is hard, so start with the simplified version). Fifteen minutes a day and your fingertips will toughen up.
OK, thanks!
Any time.
Why do cats knead?
It's a habit from nursing as kittens and usually means the cat feels relaxed and content.
OK, thanks! 🙏
Any time.
What's good to do on a rainy day?
Watch a film, tidy a room, cook a pot of soup, or just read with the rain in the background.
Thanks, that's really helpful
Glad it helped.
